SELECTED_INDEX: 1  
CONFIDENCE: 0.26  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by very strong aliphatic C–H-stretch bands at 2925 and 2980 cm⁻¹ and by an equally intense band at 767 cm⁻¹.  A powerful Raman line near 760–780 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of the breathing/rocking mode of a highly substituted bicyclic (bornane/borneol-type) skeleton; such an intense band is not expected for the acyclic alcohols (8, 9) or the small rings/heteroaromatics (3, 10).  
Candidate 1 (CC12CC(C)(C1)C2O), a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane (camphane/borneol framework) bearing three methyl groups and one hydroxyl, naturally provides:

• strong ring-breathing/bridgehead deformation near 760–780 cm⁻¹ (matches 767 cm⁻¹)  
• several C–C and C–O skeletal modes in the 900–980 cm⁻¹ region (observed 906, 927, 947, 970 cm⁻¹)  
• C–O stretching/CH wag modes around 1050–1180 cm⁻¹ (observed 1079, 1160 cm⁻¹)  
• CH₃/CH₂ deformation at 1449 cm⁻¹  
• strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2925 and 2980 cm⁻¹  

These features align with reported Raman patterns of borneol/isoborneol derivatives, whereas candidates containing additional heteroatoms (amines, diols) or lacking the rigid bicyclic frame less satisfactorily explain the very intense 767 cm⁻¹ band and the cluster of 900–980 cm⁻¹ peaks. Hence candidate 1 best matches the experimental Raman data.
